question: Should OpenClaw intentionally make backup creation fail on destinations without hard-link support in exchange for a strict no-partial, no-overwrite publication guarantee?
rationale: The branch deliberately removes an existing fallback that can be unsafe, but it changes the behavior of already-working backup destinations and cannot be resolved solely by mechanical review.

options.title: Accept fail-closed publication
options.body: Keep hard-link-only publication and document the unsupported-filesystem failure as the supported durability boundary.

options.title: Design a compatible publication mode
options.body: Preserve existing destination support only with a separately specified and tested publication contract that does not expose a partial final archive.

options.title: Pause the behavior change
options.body: Keep the current fallback until maintainers choose a cross-platform durable publication strategy.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed publication
recommendation.body: Keep hard-link-only publication and document the unsupported-filesystem failure as the supported durability boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The current member-authored branch and linked report provide the strongest available ownership signal for this backup-publication decision.
